feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 0 has no race telemetry, so the only evidence is the public contract and the rationale. The candidate is a valid, moderate baseline: five sensors spanning x = -0.03 to +0.03 m (wider than the 25 mm tape), weights -2..2 giving a signal proportional to lateral offset, kp = 2.0 (about 700 PWM difference per unit of signal), small ki and kd, and line_loss = last_direction. Nothing in it looks obviously broken, and no earlier race exists to show it is wrong. Watch three things in the race. (1) Completion time: base_speed 1.6 gives 80% of full PWM, and the course needs about 1.5 m/s average to finish in 3 s. If the run does not complete or progress stalls short of the end, raise base_speed toward 1.8 to 2.0 before touching the gains. (2) steering_oscillation and max_error: if the robot weaves on the slalom, lower kp (try 1.2 to 1.5) or raise kd (try 0.2 to 0.3) to damp the swing. If rms_error is large but oscillation is low, the robot is tracking too loosely, so raise kp in small steps. (3) line_loss_events: if they are nonzero on the slalom, widen the sensor span or change line_loss to search_left or search_right, depending on which side the robot leaves the line. Change one or two fields per revision so the cause of each change is clear.
requested_changes: If completion is 0 or completion_time is near 3 s with progress below 1, raise base_speed to 1.8 to 2.0 (base_speed 1.6 may be too slow for the 1.5 m/s average the course needs).
If steering_oscillation or max_error is high on the slalom, lower kp to 1.2 to 1.5 or raise kd to 0.2 to 0.3 to damp the swing.
If line_loss_events is nonzero, widen the sensor span (for example x = -0.04 to +0.04) or change line_loss to search_left or search_right, chosen by which side the robot leaves the line.
